summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and a specialized 3.5 Flash Cyber variant used within CodeMender, with stated efficiency, pricing, and benchmark improvements over the prior 3.5 Flash generation, while noting that pre-training for Gemini 4 has begun.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states it has begun its most ambitious pre-training run yet for the next flagship model.
mechanisms.quote: We have started our most ambitious pre-training run yet, for Gemini 4, and are excited by the progress.

mechanisms.reason: The new model is stated to require materially fewer output tokens per task at a lower cost per output token, reducing compute work per unit of output.
mechanisms.quote: it reduces output token usage by 17% compared to 3.5 Flash, and in some benchmarks like DeepSWE by Datacurve , we observe up to 65%, all at a lower cost per output token.

mechanisms.reason: The models are explicitly positioned to enable scaling of agentic workflows and high-throughput production traffic, implying more inference volume.
mechanisms.quote: Our Flash series of models is built to meet the sweet spot of efficiency and quality to enable scaling agentic workflows.

mechanisms.reason: CodeMender is described as running multiple agents in coordination to produce results, illustrating agent-executed work rather than single-seat use.
mechanisms.quote: Within CodeMender, which uses multiple 3.5 Flash Cyber agents working together to produce a single combined report, 3.5 Flash Cyber reaches competitive performance at the frontier on the popular benchmark CyberGym.

practices.reason: The release states concrete benchmark and pricing gains over the prior Flash generation that would justify migrating agentic and coding workloads to the new model.
practices.quote: 3.6 Flash delivers higher precision with fewer unwanted code edits and reduced execution loops, as seen in DeepSWE (49% vs. 37%), and shows significant improvement in ML Research, as seen in MLE Bench (63.9% vs. 49.7%).

practices.reason: The document names public benchmarks (DeepSWE, MLE Bench, OSWorld-Verified, GDPval-AA, Terminal-Bench, CyberGym) an engineering team could run to validate the model, and describes safety hardening against jailbreaks in specific risk domains.
practices.quote: 3.6 Flash is shipping with enhanced Frontier Safety safeguards in the domains of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cyber offense misuses. These safeguards make the model substantially more resistant to jailbreaks.

practices.reason: Computer use becoming a built-in client-side tool changes what an integration needs to call and monitor when using the Gemini API or Enterprise platform.
practices.quote: Computer use is now a built-in client side tool via the Gemini API and Gemini Enterprise.
